questions.question: What does HTML stand for and what is it used for?
questions.reference_answer: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language and is used to create and design web pages.

questions.question: How do web browsers interpret document structure to display text on a screen?
questions.reference_answer: Browsers parse markup tags to render headings, paragraphs, and images following DOM hierarchy.

questions.question: What instructions tell the browser which version of the markup standard is being used?
questions.reference_answer: The DOCTYPE declaration specifies the HTML standard version for the document.

Technical.title: 7 Authentication Concepts Every Developer Should Know

questions.question: Why is basic authentication considered insecure when sending credentials?
questions.reference_answer: Basic authentication sends credentials encoded in base64 without built-in encryption.

questions.question: Why are JWTs considered stateless compared to database session lookups?
questions.reference_answer: JWTs are digitally signed and contain payload claims, allowing servers to verify them locally without querying a database.

questions.question: What mechanism protects against cross-site scripting stealing auth tokens in the browser?
questions.reference_answer: Storing tokens inside HTTP-only, secure cookies prevents malicious JavaScript from accessing credentials.

questions.question: How can third-party services access files without exposing user passwords?
questions.reference_answer: OAuth 2.0 authorization grants scoped access tokens without revealing raw user credentials.

Conversational.title: Demis Hassabis: DeepMind & AI Superintelligence (Lex Fridman)

questions.question: What was the significance of AlphaFold in solving the protein folding problem?
questions.reference_answer: AlphaFold predicted 3D structures of proteins directly from amino acid sequences, solving a 50-year-old biological challenge.

questions.question: How did playing chess and board games influence Demis Hassabis's approach to AI?
questions.reference_answer: Playing chess taught him planning, intuition, and reinforcement learning strategies that inspired AlphaGo.

questions.question: What computational principles are needed to bridge artificial systems towards general human cognition?
questions.reference_answer: Integrating neural representation learning with planning, world models, and episodic memory mechanisms.

questions.question: Why is scientific discovery considered the primary long-term mission for DeepMind's models?
questions.reference_answer: Using AI as a meta-tool to accelerate breakthroughs in physics, biology, and materials science to benefit humanity.
